pages.notes: Two learning objectives inspected: sensor roles and working principles. Roadmap only; substantive content follows.

All three bullets viewed. Sensors observe environment or internal state and deliver physical-condition information. The absolute claim that robots cannot operate autonomously without sensors needs a bounded interpretation: open-loop programmed behavior can exist, but adaptation to unobserved changes is unsupported.
Transduction and all six roles viewed: perception, closed-loop control, safety, learning, localization, manipulation. Sensors provide evidence, not an automatic guarantee of stability or safety.

Both columns and every example viewed. Proprioceptive: potentiometer, encoders, IMU, joint torque, current, tachometer. Exteroceptive: cameras, LiDAR, sonar, force/tactile, GPS/GNSS. Classification follows measured role; contact force and joint torque may be related but listed separately.

All definitions viewed: range endpoints; span=max-min; signed error=measured-true; resolution; accuracy; repeatability/precision; dead band; dead time; bandwidth Hz. Dead band wording no output is shorthand for no response/change, not necessarily zero signal. Distinguish bandwidth from sample/update rate and dead time from overall latency.

All five definitions viewed: latency, output-per-input sensitivity, direction-dependent hysteresis, linearity, random noise. Proportionality wording is a simplified linearity definition; an affine calibration may include offset. Distinguish bias, noise and hysteresis; sensitivity has output/input units.

Every bullet and rotary component photo viewed. Three terminal divider uses supply, ground and wiper; linear track and negligible loading are needed for voltage proportional to position. ADC reads voltage, not angle without calibration. All four applications preserved.

Pin table 5V/GND/A0; diagram labels wiper/resistive strip/pins. Exact code A0, potValue=0, Serial.begin(9600), analogRead then println then delay(200). 0–1023 codes for 0–5V default example, 10-bit 1024 levels; distinguish quantization step from endpoint interpolation. Delay gives approximate maximum update rate ignoring overhead, not guaranteed exact sampling.

Full still photo viewed. Arduino Mega, three wires and rotary shaft connected; Serial Monitor repeatedly displays 541 at 9600 baud. Still image supports one code readout and setup, not a complete calibration curve or demonstrated response over time.

Both diagrams inspected: optical transmitter/slotted disk/receiver; four concentric absolute tracks with sixteen binary labels 0000 through1111. Four-bit example is binary labeling, not automatically Gray code. Incremental pulses need reference for absolute position; single-turn absolute angle after power-up does not automatically preserve multi-turn history.

All bullets/table and UNO illustration viewed. A to2, B to3, supply5V and GND. Phase difference gives direction; pulse counts give relative steps. Both pins are interrupt capable but following code attaches only A rising edges. Illustration is UNO even though lecture examples often say Mega; pins2/3 usable on both, not proof all board pin maps identical.

All code pixels read: volatile long count=0; PPR=600; INPUT_PULLUP pins2/3; attach only pin2 RISING; 9600 baud; noInterrupts encloses floating division count/PPR; interrupts restored before printing; Serial.println((int)rotations); delay50; ISR readsB HIGH increments else decrements. Integer cast truncates toward zero and hides fractional turns. Interrupts alone do not guarantee no lost pulses, especially masked intervals.

Full still viewed. Mega connected to rotary encoder; serial lines all Rotations: 0 at9600baud. Printed zero does not prove raw count zero because source casts fractional signed turns to int; no dynamic rotation sequence shown.

All bullets and diagram rays viewed. IR LED sends light toward surface, photodiode receives reflection; intensity fed to comparator produces digital classification. Reflectivity/angle/ambient light affect signal as well as distance; digital threshold is not a calibrated range value. Three applications line-following, obstacle avoidance and edge detection.

TableVcc5V/GND/OUT8; module photo labels VCC/GND/OUT and adjustable potentiometer. Code INPUT pin8,9600baud,digitalRead,stateHIGH prints Obstacle Detected else No Obstacle;delay300. Explicit active-high convention in code/prose must not be universalized to all module hardware.

Actual still with ruler above IR module, illuminated LED and serial history containing No Obstacle then Obstacle Detected. Do not infer exact ruler distance or hardware output polarity from photo alone. Source evidence is binary state reporting, not continuous range measurement.

Actual comparison still has no ruler above module and serial output repeatedly No Obstacle; distinct from prior figure. Both source states may be compared, but no precise threshold distance or response-time trace supplied.

All text and component labels inspected. Bright illumination reduces resistance; dim light increases it. Decreasing schematic graph has resistance in ohms and illumination in lux over multiple decades, but does not establish a universal reciprocal law or precise intermediate calibration. Diagram labels electrodes, clear coating, photoconductive material, cold-weld contacts, ceramic and wire terminals. Applications include line following, street lights, solar tracking and light-based detection.

Three-pin module table VCC5V/GND/OUTA1. Code reads analogRead(A1), prints Light Intensity then raw count, delays500ms, serial9600. High count means bright only for suitable divider orientation; bare two-lead LDR and three-pin module are distinct. No lux calibration is provided.

Actual phone flashlight illuminates the LDR module and nearby hand/table. Serial counts rise near the upper ADC range. Small blurred exact values are not transcribed as calibrated lux or exact question premises. This still demonstrates the displayed bright-condition count pattern, not a complete response curve.

Actual second still has no overhead phone illumination; serial counts remain broadly in the800s and vary. Relative comparison with prior illuminated still is consistent with this module orientation, not a universal LDR voltage polarity or calibrated irradiance curve.

Both metal-ball tube sketches viewed. One position leaves the two contacts open; tilted drawing lets ball bridge them. Two pins A/B, tilt arrow and ball positions are visible. Binary contact indicates a threshold state, not a continuous angle; mounting and acceleration matter. Applications fall detection, orientation and safety shutdown require a larger control system.

Pin table VCC5V/D0to8/GND. INPUT_PULLUP; LOW prints Tilt Detected!, else prints Tilt Not Detected! but the else Serial.println statement visibly lacks its terminating semicolon. As printed this fails compilation; explicitly repaired code must add that semicolon. No delay or debounce. Pull-up interpretation assumes a contact-to-ground or compatible module output; three-pin module is distinct from bare two-pin switch.

Actual connected Mega and handheld tilt module pictured; monitor repeatedly shows Tilt Not Detected! Empty outlined placeholder on right has no substantive data. This does not prove the preceding syntactically incomplete code compiled unchanged.
Second still shows differently oriented handheld module; monitor again displays Tilt Not Detected! It does not visibly demonstrate a transition to detected, or establish an angular threshold.

Magnetic field closes contacts in the illustrated normally-open reed switch. Diagram labels glass capsule, inert gas, contact material, glass-to-metal bond and reed blades. Door detection, wheel rotation counting and position sensing applications. A binary reed is not a continuous magnetic field meter; closure scope is illustrated type, not every reed configuration.

Pin table VCC5V/D0to9/GND; code reedPin9, INPUT_PULLUP, Serial9600. LOW prints Magnet Detected!, else Magnet Not Detected! Both semicolons present. No debounce, edge count or delay; repeated level prints are not wheel revolution counts.
Actual red module and magnet stack adjacent; green and red LEDs lit and monitor repeats Magnet Detected! No calibrated field, distance or threshold is shown.

Second actual still shows a magnet stack near module but monitor repeats Magnet Not Detected! State differs from prior slide. Orientation/history/timing are not sufficiently specified to infer a magnetic threshold or label code incorrect; still proximity alone is not calibrated evidence.

All bullets/formula and transmitter/receiver echo diagram inspected. Active non-contact40kHz example, echo-high duration for round trip, d=tc/2 with c≈343m/s. Typical0.02–4m range is example-specific, not universal. Temperature and wind matter; works in darkness/fog/dust is not environmental immunity.

HC-SR04 photo clearly labels VCC/Trig/Echo/GND. Table lists only VCC5V,TRIG9,ECHO10 and omits GND despite photo having that pin. Common reference is an explicit completion, not a printed table row. Applications obstacle detection/navigation/height-depth require geometry and controls beyond one range.

Exact visible code defines long duration/int distance, sets9OUTPUT10INPUT,9600serial. LOW2us,HIGH10us,LOW trigger; pulseIn(10,HIGH); distance=duration*0.034/2; duplicated Serial.print("Distance: ") twice, Serial.print(distance),delay300. No newline or units. Coefficient340m/s is rounded alternative to343m/s, not the same exact speed. Integer assignment truncates. No timeout/error branch.

Full setup still viewed: monitor shows separate lines with single Distance: prefix and values206/207. This display is not the exact formatting produced by p1652 duplicate-prefix/no-newline code. Demonstration is historical output, not fresh execution or calibrated ground truth.

Ruler held in front of transducers; monitor history shows207 then34. The visible sensor–ruler spacing is not a fully calibrated distance geometry; interpret change in measured echo range, not exact accuracy proof. Single-prefix line output again differs from as-printed code.

Definition ambient temperature/relative humidity. Slide explicitly says thermistor, capacitive humidity element, internal ADC, single-wire serial; humidity-element type requires primary datasheet reconciliation before endorsing. Apps environment/agriculture/weather/fire-safety-HVAC do not make DHT11 a certified fire detector.

Table VCC5V,DATA7,GND; bare four-pin drawing additionally NC. Exploded humidity-element figure labels upper/lower electrodes, moisture-holding substrate and glass substrate. NTC thermistor curve resistance decreases with temperature; schematic extreme axis labels are not DHT11 operating specifications.

All code inspected: DHT.h, DHTPIN7,DHTTYPE DHT11,DHT object; setup Serial9600,dht.begin; reads humidity and temperature floats, prints Humidity value percent then Temperature value degreesC with final println;delay2000. No isnan/error branch. Two-second delay plus work is not an exact guaranteed sampling period.

Actual blue sensor module/Mega and serial historical outputs. Humidity44.00 then43.00 percent; temperatures28.70/28.80C visible. Displayed decimals are formatting, not proof0.01 accuracy/resolution; no reference instrument or calibration shown.

Text, board axes and arrows inspected. Accelerometer/gyro/optional magnetometer; unitsm/s²,degrees/s,microtesla; I2C example. Accelerometer linear-acceleration shorthand needs specific-force/gravity qualification. Gyro rate not direct orientation, magnetometer field not guaranteed undisturbed heading. Board diagram indicates signed axes; applications balancing/drones/navigation/gestures.

Table labeled MPU6500:VCC5V,SDA20,SCL21,GND. Illustration labelsVCC/GND/SCL/SDA/XDA/XCL/AD0/INT but does not establish bare-chip5V tolerance. Code Wire.h,MPU_ADDR0x68,int16_t ax ay az,float tiltAngle,offset0. Supply must be compatible breakout not bare-chip assumption.

Exact code Serial115200,Wire.begin,writes0x00 to0x6B,wake;delay2000,offset=readTilt,Calibration done. Loop readTilt minusoffset,Lower leg tilt degrees,delay50. readTilt atan2(-ax,sqrt((float)ay*ay+(float)az*az))*180/PI. readAccel selects0x3B,repeated-start endTransmission(false),requests6bytes then combines paired Wire.read()<<8|Wire.read for eachaxis. Need explicit high-byte-first sequential reconstruction for portable checks because operand evaluation order is not a portable stream-read guarantee. No available/status checks. Gravity-dominated static posture and calibrated frame needed; no gyro/magnetometer fusion.

Actual handheld blue board labeled MPU-9250/6500 is connected; monitor displays Tilt Angle rather than printed Lower leg tilt prefix. Exact blurred angle values are not used. A breakout photo cannot certify the chip model, voltage tolerance or heading observability.

Board taped to upright metal bottle, monitor shows Tilt Angle values near zero with positive and negative variation. This supports calibrated relative pitch display, not zero noise or proof of roll/yaw/translation accuracy. Ruler is present but no controlled angular reference.

All text inspected. Header namesVL53L0X while body describes general scanning LiDAR and point clouds. Range plus beam direction/scan angles and sensor pose allow coordinates; a single-zone fixed VL53L0X does not itself provide a rotating2D/3D cloud. Distinguish general ToF principle from product capabilities.

Formula d=tc/2,c=3×10^8m/s; emission/reflection/photodetection diagram. 2D single rotating plane, example360degrees,0.1–40m,10–40Hz;3D multiple channels example64beam,100k–2Mpoints/s. These ranges/rates are illustrative device-class values, not VL53L0X specs or universal sensor limits.

All applications and table inspected. SDA20,SCL21,VIN5V,GND. Photo labelsVIN/GND/SCL/SDA and53L0X. These are I2C pins;5V refers compatible breakoutVIN rather than bare-chip supply. Obstacle/navigation/inspection/SLAM are system applications, not stand-alone localization output.

Exact code Wire.h and Adafruit_VL53L0X.h;Serial9600,Wire.begin;failedbegin prints notdetected then while(1),successReady. Loop rangingTest(&measure,false),RangeStatus!=4 prints RangeMilliMeter/10.0cm;else Outofrange;delay300. Right-hand explanation incorrectly claims UART/SoftwareSerial though neither SoftwareSerial include nor object appears; sensor bus is I2C, Serial is host output. Not-equal4 is literal filter, not proof every other status is valid.

Actual module/Mega/ruler still; historical serial Distance16.30,16.10,15.30,14.60,14.70,14.80cm among visible readings. Decimal formatting is consistent with mm divided10.0 but not0.01cm accuracy. No point cloud, scan angle or full calibration is shown.

A1M8 description and cutaway drawing inspected: motor rotates emitter, encoder tracks angle, thousands samples/s,2D data,USB/UART,SLAM/indoor navigation. This page itself does not claim ToF; do not incorrectly attribute prior generic ToF text as an explicit claim here. Need range+angle for planar coordinates and pose for map frame.

Steps connectUSB,install driver,openViewer,selectCOM,startscan. Output360scan,distance-angle plot claimed red,0.2–6m radius, resolution<0.5mm (1% ofdistance),angular≤1degree. Absolute and percentage resolution cannot be treated as equivalent throughout range. Specs require model/version conditions; no invented universal limit.

Actual viewer polar graph viewed.0degreesup,90right,180down,270left; cyan/green returns, red top status text. Display says6.9Hz(416RPM),8K,Current186.00Deg:259.11. Plot color is not universally red as prior prose says.6.9Hz and416RPM compatible rounded values. No explicit unit for259.11 visible so do not assign without premise.

Six modality rows inspected: monocular lacks native depth,stereo disparity,RGB-D,color+depth,fisheye/360ultrawide,thermalIR,asynchronous event brightness change. Approx5m stereo reliability,<1ms event latency,>180degreeFOV are illustrative not universal guarantees. RGB-D can have invalid/unregistered pixels. Thermal is emitted heat signature, not active reflectiveIR obstacle module.

Every working-principle bullet viewed. Lens→photodiode charge→colorfilter sampling→ADC→processor image. More light stronger signal assumes fixed exposure/gain and unsaturated response. Bayer RGB described but no actual2×2 pattern shown; any numeric Bayer mosaic premise must be explicitly supplied. Not every camera requires Bayer or millions of pixels.

All seven application categories viewed: smartphone,automotive,medical,satellite,CCTV,roboticsAI,industrial inspection. Image processing enhances/extracts/detects; image quality is not identical to task accuracy. Questions should select sensor/processing for bounded robotic tasks rather than memorize nontechnical labels.

Five numbered stages camera capture,CNNprocessing,detection,boxes,labels/confidence. Person/car/bicycle/bus examples. Real-time is performance aspiration not guaranteed by CPUlarge model. Bounding box is2D localization, not metric3D position; confidence is model score not guaranteed probability or dataset precision.
